entry: src/runtime/agent/orchestrator/providers/openai-ws-send-attempts.mjs createWsSendAttempts(opts) / openai-ws-send/send-context.mjs createWsSendContext(opts), provider-error-kind.mjs retryReasonClass / safeRetryErrorCode, retry-executor.mjs emitProviderRetryStage, stall-policy.mjs providerTimeoutError. The state-machine cases feed a scripted Error (own properties are the inputs) and read `attempts.state` and the error objects after each call; the `ws-*` cases run sendViaWebSocket over a real loopback WebSocket.
exclusions: ORDER RULE (one of the orders Node allows): before each retry step the recorder waits until every connection opened so far is closed at the server, so a connection the client released after a failed attempt has its `closed` event (serverInitiated false, reason release_no_keep) recorded before the retry's `stage: requesting` and its dial. Node does not guarantee that order: releaseWebSocket only requests the close and returns (src/runtime/agent/orchestrator/providers/openai-ws-pool.mjs:937), so the close may complete before or after the retry starts. Pairs covered (11): ws-rate-limited-response-failed-waits-advised-time (1), ws-long-advised-wait-announced-before-it-starts (1), ws-server-error-text-never-reaches-retry-stage (3), ws-retry-stage-carries-known-codes-never-failure-text sends 0, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 (1 each): each is a `closed` (serverInitiated false) entry immediately followed by a `stage` requesting entry. Comparison rule for a replay: within each such pair either order is equal; everything else is compared in recorded order. Because the close completes before the clock moves, the ws client's 30 s close timer (node_modules/ws/lib/websocket.js:1324-1326 setCloseTimer, cleared at :1368 once the close completes) is cancelled before the advance and does not appear among the fired timers of the clock steps

auth-token-refresh-stalls-past-its-timeout-classifies-as-auth (:345): the recorded answer is what the product path gives, reasonClass "other" (stage reason "Connection interrupted"). The cited test asserts "auth" one level lower: it hands retryReasonClass (provider-error-kind.mjs:767, `timeoutPhase === auth`) the inner timeout error that exchangeRefreshToken throws (openai-oauth-tokens.mjs:278-280, timeoutPhase auth). On the product path refreshStoredTokens -> refreshUnderLock catches it and throws a new Error("OpenAI OAuth token refresh failed (...). Re-authenticate via provider login.") (openai-oauth-tokens.mjs:354) that copies reauth fields only for a permanent refusal and carries neither timeoutPhase nor a cause, so the class the test asserts is not what a caller of the refresh receives
